segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics News Digest for October 20th, 2026.
Today we cover big moves like the Navy contract, Waymo's Spanish expansion, and exciting humanoid advancements.
From The Robot Report, Gecko Robotics secures $300 million contract with the U.S.
Navy.
This report details the acquisition of an additional three hundred million dollars in contract value for the U.S.
Navy and GSA to enhance fleet readiness and decrease maintenance delays.
The company's artificial intelligence and robotic technology, specifically the Komodo system, is utilized to identify structural issues up to fifty times faster than conventional assessment methods.
This capability enables damage assessment without the need for stripping deck coatings, resulting in significant cost savings for the Navy during repairs.
The expanded contract directly supports the Navy's objective of reaching eighty percent fleet readiness through the acceleration of inspection processes.
This development signals increased adoption of advanced robotics in maritime infrastructure inspection.
From Waymo Blog, "¡Llegamos a Madrid! Waymo is coming to Spain".
This report details the initiation of Waymo's fully autonomous ride-hailing service deployment in Spain, commencing with the Region of Madrid.
Waymo plans to introduce its service to riders in 2027 through a phased approach that prioritizes safety, beginning with manual driving validation.
The company is actively collaborating with Spanish authorities and investing in local operations to ensure alignment with regional and national safety objectives.

Data from Waymo Driver indicates that the autonomous technology has been involved in ninety-five percent fewer crashes involving serious injury or worse than human drivers, aiming to improve urban mobility by mitigating accidents resulting from human error.
This development signals a step toward integrating advanced autonomous technology into public transportation networks across the continent.
From Robotics & Automation News, Agility Robotics’ new Digit humanoid to work 20 hours a day with Nyobolt fast-charging battery.
This report details a partnership between Agility Robotics and Nyobolt to upgrade the Digit 5 humanoid robot with a fast-charging battery system, enabling extended operational time.
The new battery technology facilitates a nine-minute charge for a ninety-minute runtime, establishing a ten to one run-to-charge ratio.
This advancement directly addresses previous power limitations that restricted the economics of autonomous robot fleets in warehouse and manufacturing settings.
The enhanced battery performance is projected to increase the value proposition of the Digit 5 platform for industrial applications.
This development signals a step forward in improving the practical viability of autonomous robotics in commercial environments.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build".

This report details the development of Digit 5, the first humanoid robot designed for safe and economic work in warehouses, achieving the capability to lift twenty-three-kilogram bins while operating safely near human coworkers through proximity sensors.

The development process prioritized customer needs and safety regulations over an initial purely graceful design, resulting in a larger, more functional robot that balances commercial viability with the pursuit of human-like motion.
This engineering approach established a practical foundation for future advancements in fully agile and dexterous humanoid robotics.
The successful deployment of Digit 5 indicates a tangible step toward applying advanced robotics in industrial settings.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, "Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world".
This report details how the company utilizes automated red-teaming systems to stress-test physical artificial intelligence for robotics and autonomous vehicles prior to actual deployment.
The methodology involves constructing high-fidelity simulations grounded in real-world data, employing AI agents to actively probe for potential failure points.
These agents use real-world data, such as news and police reports, to design challenging corner cases, thereby stress-testing autonomous systems.
This process seeks to establish a shared foundation of evidence regarding safety and foster greater trust among stakeholders.
Laplace is developing a dynamic interactive testing process as a new framework for physical AI safety.
This development establishes a rigorous testing paradigm for ensuring the safety of autonomous physical systems entering the market.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Automation Created a Training Problem: Upskilling the Industrial Workforce".
This report details the skills gap created by automation, noting that the demand for new competencies frequently outpaces the availability of traditional training.
The necessity for workers to acquire skills in operating, maintaining, and programming automated systems is not adequately addressed by current training structures.

Digital e-learning methods are proving effective for disseminating knowledge among shift-based workforces, although practical, hands-on practice is still considered essential for achieving full competence.
Successful workforce upskilling mandates the direct integration of training planning within the automation project timeline.
Manufacturers must prioritize workforce development by budgeting it alongside hardware to ensure the realization of automation productivity gains.
This indicates that integrating continuous skills development is a prerequisite for maximizing the return on investment in technological automation.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Toyota Material Handling says digital twins can halve autonomous forklift commissioning time".

This report details how Toyota Material Handling is employing digital twin technology to significantly accelerate the development and commissioning of autonomous forklifts, achieving a potential reduction in commissioning effort by up to fifty percent and shortening the time-to-market by forty percent.
The process utilizes Nvidia Omniverse and Isaac Sim to virtually test autonomous vehicle systems within simulated factory environments.
Digital twins enable teams to test navigation, safety logic, and real-world interactions, facilitating early issue resolution and minimizing the need for on-site adjustments.
Furthermore, the methodology incorporates machine vision using synthetic data to enhance object detection capabilities for pallet handling systems.
This advancement demonstrates a method for drastically reducing the physical testing requirements in robotics deployment.
The integration of simulation into hardware development sets a new benchmark for industrial automation timelines.
From Robotics & Automation News, "What robot builders overlook about cooling compact servo drives and controllers".
This report examines the complex thermal management challenges encountered in compact robotic systems due to restricted airflow around multiple heat-generating electronic components.
Effective thermal design necessitates evaluating system-level performance based on actual operating conditions, including peak loads and duty cycles, instead of relying solely on component ratings.
Heat sink selection must be based on a calculated thermal budget, taking into account the thermal interface and mounting surface quality.
Forced-air cooling effectiveness is constrained by internal restrictions, and the mechanical mounting interface directly influences heat transfer.
Reliable thermal management requires early collaboration among thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to achieve practical and dependable solutions.
This emphasis on system-level thermal analysis is crucial for the advancement of compact robotics in the technology sector.
From The Robot Report, "Kodama raises $7M to bring robotics to forestry".
This story concerns Kodama's successful fundraising effort to advance physical artificial intelligence within the forestry industry, achieving a capital raise of seven million dollars.
Kodama employs a hybrid approach combining supervised autonomy and teleoperation to augment machine capabilities during commercial logging operations in the southeastern United States.
The technology has demonstrated the capacity for machinery to move over one hundred thousand tons of timber in these operations.
The company is currently integrating with existing Original Equipment Manufacturers to utilize established machine knowledge and establish a data advantage.
This data collection process is designed to improve on-site productivity and enhance safety for forestry personnel.
This development signals continued investment in applied AI solutions for heavy industry and suggests a focus on real-world operational improvements in resource management.
From Robotics & Automation News, ABB Robotics introduces two new high-performance robots for precision manufacturing.
This report details the launch of the IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID robots, which demonstrate significant improvements in cycle time and operational efficiency for precision manufacturing tasks.
The newly introduced robots offer up to twenty percent shorter cycle times compared to comparable models, directly enhancing productivity.

These systems are equipped with payloads ranging from six to twelve kilograms, maintain a high precision repeatability of zero point zero three millimeters, and achieve joint speeds up to seven hundred degrees per second.
Furthermore, these advancements incorporate measures to reduce operating costs, featuring up to fifteen percent lower power consumption and extended service intervals.
These specifications position the robots for demanding applications such as arc welding and novel electronics assembly.
The introduction signals a continued push towards higher efficiency and greater precision within the robotics and automation sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, "New ASTM standard aims to test how robots perform in the real world".

This report details the development of a new standard by ASTM International to measure the performance of robotic manipulators and mobile manipulators under conditions of controlled optical-signal degradation.
The proposed methodology quantifies the impact of degraded optical information on a robot's task completion capabilities in simulated real-world settings.
Degradation caused by factors such as fluctuating light or interference is examined to determine how it affects downstream machine-learning models and the potential for task failure or safety risks.

This standard seeks to establish a repeatable method for testing performance under stress to identify system limitations prior to deployment, supporting responsible real-world integration and contributing to UN Sustainable Development Goal number eight.
The development provides a framework for rigorously assessing robotic performance in complex environments.
From The Robot Report, Daimon Robotics building the infrastructure layer for tactile intelligence.
This report details the development of a framework connecting tactile sensing, data collection, simulation, and artificial intelligence models for tactile intelligence.
The company is developing a pipeline to process tactile feedback at thirty Hertz, which links real-world data with simulations to effectively bridge the simulation to reality gap.
This infrastructure supports manipulation tasks that necessitate robots reacting to physical contact, including assembly and packaging.
The objective is to create a tactile-grounded world model enabling robots to reason about physical interactions beyond visual perception.
This work indicates a focus on creating a foundational layer for advanced robotic reasoning systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Tesollo robotic hand sales set to surpass 1,000 units in 2026.
This report details the projected sales trajectory for Tesollo's robotic hands and grippers, forecasting a cumulative sale volume exceeding one thousand units by the close of 2026.

Tesollo, a South Korean robotics company, anticipates this growth is fueled by escalating demand within the fields of humanoid robotics, physical artificial intelligence, and industrial automation requiring flexible end-effectors.
The company has responded to this demand by expanding its production facilities and manufacturing infrastructure to sustain the anticipated global requirement.

Tesollo currently provides a range of articulated hands featuring one to five fingers utilized in both research and industrial settings, with plans underway to further enhance manufacturing capabilities and explore a potential public listing in South Korea.
This development signals continued momentum in the market for sophisticated robotic end-effectors within advanced technology sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, Schaeffler opened a humanoid factory in Taicang deploying six robots on a joint module assembly line.
This facility integrates robot component production, humanoid training, and industrial deployment.
The 7,500 square meter facility features robots performing tasks including material handling, sorting, fitting, inspection, and packaging.
The operation incorporates six training scenarios and utilizes a digital twin system to connect training with production validation.
Schaeffler plans for the location to function as a collaboration platform for various Chinese robotics companies.
This development signals an expansion in the practical application and industrial integration of humanoid robotics technology.
Further developments in collaborative robotics are anticipated in this sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "SPD robot training pairs virtual practice with real demos".
This report details a method for developing dexterous bimanual policies in robots using simulated demonstrations combined with real-world data.
Five individuals collected seventy-five hours of demonstrations within a five-six-degree-of-freedom simulated system across various scenes and objects, generating data for two arms and two hands.
This data was used to pretrain a two-hundred-twenty-two-million-parameter diffusion transformer policy before adapting it to actual data.
The simulation pretraining demonstrated superior performance compared to behavior cloning for these tasks, providing a tangible evaluation signal.
This advancement suggests a more effective approach for training complex robotic manipulation skills in realistic environments.

From turingpost.com, Twitter Library featuring Turing Post provides curated content on artificial intelligence concepts, including model architectures, reinforcement learning approaches, and agentic memory, presented through infographics.
The platform details advancements in embodied AI and robotics, AI agent frameworks, and developments in large language model attention mechanisms.
The content also reviews open-source tools pertaining to AI guardrails, retrieval augmented generation, and various AI model types, tracking research in LLMs, AI agents, and AI infrastructure.
This library aims to offer precise analysis for engineers, researchers, and founders focused on machine learning and artificial intelligence functionality.
The focus on practical applications and open-source tools indicates an ongoing trend toward deployable, transparent, and modular AI systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Primepick brings NSF-certified robotic hot-meal kiosk to the US market, detailing the expansion of its MealMate system into new locations across the United States.

The robotic hot-meal kiosk is designed to serve hot dishes in five to seven minutes and is being deployed in settings including hospitals, nursing homes, and new sites in Huntsville, Chicago, and Dallas.

This system employs robotic arms, specialized storage, and proprietary software for automated management and inventory, facilitating access to hot meals outside traditional foodservice hours without the need for on-site kitchen staff.
The marketplace model connects customers directly with meals sourced from local restaurants and dark kitchens.
This development signals further integration of automated food preparation technologies into institutional and commercial food service environments.
And that's all the circuits for today from the Robotics Digest!
Gecko Robotics just snagged a massive Navy contract – talkin' big hardware!
Thanks for powering up your day with us.
See you tomorrow!
